claim: Anic, Barbon, Seiz and Zarattini (2025, arXiv:2510.26228) report that in the out-of-sample period (Jan 2024-Mar 2025, after ChatGPT 4.0 mini's Oct 2023 pre-training cutoff), the LLM-enhanced momentum strategy's Sharpe ratio is 1.06 versus 0.79 for the baseline momentum strategy, net of 2bps costs.
quote: The Sharpe ratio improves from 0.79 for the baseline to 1.06 for the LLM-enhanced strategy
limitations: OOS window is only 15 months and contains no crisis/drawdown period; the paper's own LLM-vs-baseline alpha regression is significant only at the 10% level.
independent_replication: Not yet independently replicated (posted 2025-10-30); this round is itself an independent replication attempt on a different (US PIT largest-500, DeepSeek-scored) data and model setup.
impact_on_spec: Sets the informational comparison target for L's OOS Sharpe and grounds the look-ahead-control design (clean window must start after the scoring model's own cutoff, mirroring the paper's Oct-2023-cutoff logic).

claim: The paper's re-weighting rule for the LLM-enhanced portfolio is Wi = E * eta^LLM_Score_i, where E is the baseline (equal- or value-weight) share, LLM_Score_i is the score normalized to [-1, 1], and eta is a scaling parameter optimized to 5 on the validation set; weights are then renormalized to sum to one, with an optional 15% per-stock cap.
limitations: The PDF text extraction renders the exponent as plain text ("eta LLM_Scorei") with the superscript lost; read as an exponential tilt (Wi = E * eta^score_i) because (a) eta is described as a 'scaling parameter' and 'weight multiplier', (b) scores range over [-1, 1] so a linear eta*score would make some baseline-positive weights negative for a long-only book, which the paper never discusses, and (c) an exponential form keeps every weight positive across the full score range (eta^-1=0.2x to eta^1=5x at eta=5), matching the paper's own description of eta=5 as indicating a 'meaningful' and 'confidently exploited' dynamic range. No appendix with a clearer typeset formula was found in the 26-page PDF.
independent_replication: Not independently replicated; this is this round's own reading of the primary source.
impact_on_spec: L's per-stock weight is computed as Wi = E * eta^score_i (eta=5), 15% cap, renormalized to sum 1; E is fixed to equal weight (1/m) rather than the paper's own optimal value-weighted E, disclosed as a deviation because this repo has no reliable point-in-time market-cap feature and because using the same equal-weight E as baseline B isolates the LLM re-ranking/tilt effect.

claim: The paper's validation-set-optimal hyperparameter configuration selects monthly rebalancing, a 1-day news lookback, a 21-day lookahead, the 'basic' prompt, m=50 selected stocks, a 15% per-stock weight cap, value-weighted initial allocation, and eta=5.
quote: The optimal number of stocks selected each month is m = 50
limitations: Optimal on the paper's own S&P 500 / ChatGPT-4o-mini validation set (Oct 2019-Dec 2023); not re-optimized for our universe, DeepSeek model, or cost assumptions -- used as preregistered, not tuned, per this round's anti-overfitting rule.
impact_on_spec: L uses m=50 unchanged from the paper. This round's own lookback (30 days, cap 20 headlines) and rebalance (monthly) deviate from the paper's optimal 1-day lookback -- disclosed deviation, since a 1-day news lookback would leave most candidate-months with zero qualifying headlines given this repo's lower news density outside mega-caps.

claim: When a stock-day has no relevant news, the paper treats the missing LLM score as zero (on the normalized [-1, 1] scale), representing a neutral stance.
quote: those missing scores are treated as zero, reflecting a neutral stance in the absence of new information
limitations: Described for the daily-score panel used in the paper's summary statistics, not stated separately for the monthly-rebalance production rule, but is the only no-news rule the paper states.
impact_on_spec: A candidate with zero qualifying anonymized headlines in the 30-day lookback gets a normalized score of 0 (raw 0.5) without a DeepSeek call, per the brief's own preregistered fallback and the paper's rule.

claim: The paper extends the baseline top-decile 12-1 momentum candidate set to also include the second decile before LLM scoring, and its output format asks for a single 0-1 score where 0 means momentum will stop/revert and 1 means momentum will continue.
quote: we consider those in the top decile of past 12-month returns, excluding the most recent month
limitations: Describes the baseline (decile 1) definition the extended pool is built from; the second-decile extension is described narratively in the same section, not as a separately quotable single sentence.
impact_on_spec: Grounds B (top decile) and L/P/R's candidate pool (top-2 deciles) of the PIT largest-500 universe.

claim: The paper's basic prompt asks the model to output a single score from 0 to 1, where 0 means momentum will stop or revert and 1 means momentum will continue, conditioned on the stock being about to enter a momentum portfolio.
quote: The prediction is expressed as a score from 0 to 1, where 0 means the momentum will stop
limitations: Copied from the paper's basic-prompt worked example (AAPL, 5-day lookback, 21-day horizon); this round adapts the ticker, lookback (30 days) and horizon (to next month-end) per stock-month.
impact_on_spec: scripts/score_h20260928_22_news_momentum.py's DeepSeek prompt reuses this exact task/output-format wording, adapted with the anonymized ticker and dates.

claim: All of the paper's reported results assume 2 basis points of transaction costs per trade, and the out-of-sample period begins after ChatGPT 4.0 mini's October 2023 pre-training cutoff, so its performance cannot be attributed to memorization of the outcome.
quote: it begins after the October 2023 pre-training cut-off of ChatGPT 4.0 mini
limitations: 2bps is materially lower than this repo's 10/20bp contract; reported as the paper's own (more favorable) assumption alongside our own stricter cost views.
impact_on_spec: Directly motivates this round's own look-ahead control: the CLEAN window must start at the first month-end after DeepSeek's own disclosed knowledge cutoff, not before.

claim: arXiv:2510.26228 ('ChatGPT in Systematic Investing -- Enhancing Risk-Adjusted Returns with LLMs' by Nikolas Anic, Andrea Barbon, Ralf Seiz and Carlo Zarattini) was submitted 30 Oct 2025 to q-fin.PM (Portfolio Management).
quote: [Submitted on 30 Oct 2025] Title: ChatGPT in Systematic Investing
limitations: Abstract page only confirms existence, authorship and submission date, not the results themselves (see the fulltext-extract snapshot for those claims).
independent_replication: arXiv preprint server listing; cross-checked against the SSRN/SFI working-paper listing found by the earlier I-20260928-03 intel pass (SSRN 5680782).
impact_on_spec: Confirms the paper's identity, authorship and date for citation.

claim: Glasserman & Lin (2023, arXiv:2309.17322) find that removing a company's identifiers from news text before LLM sentiment scoring (anonymization) improves in-sample trading performance versus using the original headlines, indicating the 'distraction effect' (general knowledge about the named company interfering with sentiment measurement) has a larger impact than look-ahead bias for their sample.
quote: We compare trading performance based on the original headlines with de-biased strategies in which we remove the relevant company's identifiers from the text.
limitations: Findings are for GPT sentiment scoring of news headlines on a different (older GPT, different universe) setup; motivates our anonymization design, not a direct performance transfer.
independent_replication: Also referenced by arXiv:2601.13770 (Look-Ahead-Bench) and arXiv:2512.23847 as a standard anonymization-bias baseline, per this round's web search.
impact_on_spec: scripts/score_h20260928_22_news_momentum.py anonymizes every headline (company name and ticker replaced with 'the company') for both L and P, following this paper's method, before sending text to DeepSeek.

claim: He, Lv, Manela and Wu (2025, arXiv:2502.21206) show that LLM training data can introduce lookahead bias and training leakage in social-science and financial applications, and that lookahead bias is model- and application-specific -- motivating chronologically consistent (only-past-data) training and, by extension, evaluation windows that start strictly after a model's own disclosed knowledge cutoff.
quote: only the text data that would have been available at each point in time
limitations: Proposes training chronologically consistent models (ChronoBERT/ChronoGPT) rather than post-hoc cutoff-based evaluation of an off-the-shelf model; we use the weaker (but only locally feasible) control of restricting the verdict window to after the model's disclosed cutoff, disclosed as a limitation relative to their approach.
independent_replication: Cited directly by Anic et al. (2025, our target paper, reference list) as grounding for the same OOS-cutoff logic.
impact_on_spec: Grounds the CLEAN-vs-contaminated window split and the requirement to report contaminated months separately, never counting them toward the verdict.

claim: Third-party model-catalog aggregator Puter states DeepSeek V4 Flash has a knowledge cutoff of April 2026 and a release date of April 24, 2026.
quote: Knowledge Cutoff Apr 2026 Release Date Apr 24, 2026
limitations: Third-party aggregator, not DeepSeek's own documentation; DeepSeek's own API docs (news260424 announcement, updates changelog -- both fetched below) confirm the April 24, 2026 release date and parameter counts but do not themselves state an explicit knowledge-cutoff date, so this is currently the best available disclosed cutoff and is treated conservatively (the CLEAN window starts at the first month-end AFTER, not including, this date).
independent_replication: Release date corroborated independently by DeepSeek's own official changelog/announcement pages (deepseek_v4_announce, deepseek_v4_updates cards below).
impact_on_spec: Sets the CLEAN window start: first month-end after April 2026, i.e. formation 2026-05-29 onward.

claim: DeepSeek's official API docs changelog lists DeepSeek-V4 Preview Release with DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T total / 49B active params) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B total / 13B active params), dated 2026/04/24.
limitations: Confirms model identity, size and release date but not an explicit knowledge-cutoff date (see deepseek_v4_flash_knowledge_cutoff_puter card for the cutoff figure used).
independent_replication: Official DeepSeek documentation; primary source for the model's existence and release date.
impact_on_spec: Confirms the exact model identity behind OC_TEXT_SCORER_MODEL=Deepseek-v4-flash (the base V4-Flash, not a later Vision/1.1 variant).

claim: DeepSeek's official changelog shows DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash was released 2026-09-10 (newer than the base V4-Flash, released 2026-04-24) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp on 2026-08-21 -- distinct, later model versions from the base 'DeepSeek-V4-Flash' this repo's endpoint is configured to (per the model id 'Deepseek-v4-flash', with no '.1' or 'vision' suffix).
quote: Today, we officially release the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model.
limitations: Does not itself state whether the account's configured endpoint has since been silently upgraded from base V4-Flash to V4.1-Flash server-side; treated as a disclosed uncertainty, the more conservative (earlier, April 2026) cutoff is used for the CLEAN window either way.
independent_replication: Consistent with the release-date table on the deepseek_v4_announce card (same document family).
impact_on_spec: Supports using the more conservative April 2026 cutoff (base V4-Flash) rather than the newer September 2026 V4.1-Flash cutoff for the CLEAN window boundary.

claim: Alpaca's historical news API provides news data dating back to 2015, averaging 130+ articles per day, currently supplied by Benzinga.
quote: This API provides historical news data dating back to 2015. You can expect to receive an average of 130+ news articles per day. All news data is currently provided directly by Benzinga
limitations: Does not itself establish immutable first-seen timestamps or revision history; this repo's local data/features/news_packets carries its own fetched_at/visible_at fields used for the actual PIT cutoff, not this page's claim alone.
independent_replication: Same claim already verified and reused in this repo's mom_pit_semantic_theme_r11 source cards (dynamic_theme_alpaca_news_history, r11_alpaca_news_api_contract); re-fetched fresh here for this iteration's own freshness window.
impact_on_spec: Confirms the news_packets data source (Alpaca/Benzinga) used to build L and P's headline inputs, with visible_at as the point-in-time cutoff field.
